title: The wire beater for the cymbal and two-handed bass drumming
summary: Glass credits Black Benny with the cymbal beater, says he made one, and compares it with two-handed school band drumming.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Who do you think invented that wire beater for the cymbal? You know, the beater that gives it the- What I got? Who's the first one to ever make that?
Well I seen Black Banner with that.
Yeah I seen Black Banner with that. I made one. I made that. And put the cymbal on the top of it.
What did the other drummers use?

Did they have anything like that? No, some of them didn't. I never seen them with it. But they started using it now, you know? Because that answers for the music, you have to have that cymbal, that brass. Some of the other bands, they'd have two cymbals. They'd have a band, they'd have them two cymbals slapped together. They'd have a man just to play that cymbal.
In other words they made that to take the place of a man.
Yeah, it may take the place of a man, you see?
You ever see a two-handed bass drummer down here? Yeah.
We have them school band there. The school band, that's what they're using now. All the school just playing that two-hand with the bass drum.
But the old timers didn't do that?

No, no. This is new, the schools coming up with this is new. Now, I can do what they do with that, with that, them two hands, I can take that, take my one hand on that beater, and that cymbal and do this what they're doing.
You double-dipping. Oh yeah, I can do that.
Of course, well it looks like it's cutting a man out, you know? It's in order.
